
 
# ng-magic-test-bed
> Streamlined Angular unit test setup utility. Replaces verbose `TestBed.configureTestingModule` boilerplate with a fluent, type-safe API. Uses Jasmine spies automatically. Automatically extends all mocks with all methods of the class to be mocked.
Docs: https://peejay-solutions.github.io/ng-magic-test-bed/
## Installation
```bash
npm install @peejay-solutions/ng-magic-test-bed --save-dev
```
## Core Usage Pattern
```typescript
import { NgMagicSetupTestBed } from '@peejay-solutions/ng-magic-test-bed';
describe('MyService', () => {
  function setup() {
    const magic = new NgMagicSetupTestBed();
    const depMock = magic.serviceMock(DependencyService);
    const service = magic.injection(MyService);
    return { service, depMock };
  }
  it('should do X when Y', () => {
    const { service, depMock } = setup();
    depMock.someMethod.and.returnValue('value');
    expect(service.doSomething()).toBe('expected');
  });
});
```
`magic.injection()` triggers TestBed configuration — call it after all mocks are set up.
---
## NgMagicSetupTestBed API
### Module Setup (call before injection)
| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `declaration(c)` / `declarations(cs)` | Add component/directive/pipe to declarations |
| `import(m)` / `imports(ms)` | Add module to imports |
| `provider(p)` / `providers(ps)` | Add provider |
| `schema(s)` / `schemas(ss)` | Add schema (`NO_ERRORS_SCHEMA` included by default) |
### Mocking
**`serviceMock<S>(serviceClass, mock?, dontSpy?)`**
Creates and registers a mock for a service. All methods from serviceClass will be added to mock. All methods are auto-spied.
```typescript
// Auto-generated spy mock (no custom mock needed)
const myServiceMock = magic.serviceMock(MyService);
myServiceMock.getData.and.returnValue(of([]));
// Custom partial mock (methods are still wrapped in spies)
const myServiceMock = magic.serviceMock(MyService, new MyServiceMock());
```
**`providerMock<M>(token, mock, dontSpy?, spySource?)`**
Mocks an injection token.
**`objectMock<O>(objectClass, mock, dontSpy?)`**
Creates a mock object without TestBed registration (for manual use).
**`factoryMock<I, F>(factoryClass, instances)`**
Mocks a factory service whose `create()` method returns sequential instances from the provided array.
```typescript
const instance1 = { value: 'a' };
const instance2 = { value: 'b' };
magic.factoryMock(MyFactory, [instance1, instance2]);
// first call to factory.create() returns instance1, second returns instance2
```
**`componentServiceMock<S>(componentClass, serviceClass, mock?, dontSpy?)`**
Mocks a service provided at the component level (not root).
**`directiveServiceMock<S>(directiveClass, serviceClass, mock?, dontSpy?)`**
Mocks a service provided at the directive level.
**`pipeServiceMock<S>(pipeClass, serviceClass, mock?, dontSpy?)`**
Mocks a service provided at the pipe level.
**`componentProviderMock<M>(componentClass, token, mock, dontSpy?)`**
Mocks an injection token provided by a specific component.
**`directiveProviderMock<M>(directiveClass, token, mock, dontSpy?)`**
Mocks an injection token provided by a specific directive.
**`pipeProviderMock<M>(pipeClass, token, mock, dontSpy?)`**
Mocks an injection token provided by a specific pipe.
### Injection & Fixtures
**`injection<S>(token)`**
Resolves a service/class from DI. Triggers TestBed compilation — call after all mocks are registered.
```typescript
const service = magic.injection(MyService);
```
**`fixture<C>(componentClass, initialInputs?, disableNoErrorSchema?)`**
Creates a `ComponentFixture<C>`. **May only be called once per `NgMagicSetupTestBed` instance.**
- `initialInputs` — a `Partial<C>` object whose properties are applied to `componentInstance` **before** the first `detectChanges()`. This is the correct way to set `@Input()` values that are required in `ngOnInit`.
- `disableNoErrorSchema` — by default `NO_ERRORS_SCHEMA` is added so unknown child elements/inputs are silently ignored. Pass `true` to disable this and get strict template checking.
- Returns a standard Angular `ComponentFixture<C>` (same as `TestBed.createComponent()`).
- Call after all mocks and `componentMocks`/`directiveMocks` are registered.
```typescript
// Basic fixture with initial inputs
const fixture = magic.fixture(MyComponent, { label: 'test', count: 42 });
expect(fixture.componentInstance.label).toBe('test');
// Full component test pattern
function setup() {
  const magic = new NgMagicSetupTestBed();
  const childMocks = magic.componentMocks(MyChildComponentMock);
  const serviceMock = magic.componentServiceMock(MyComponent, MyService, new MyServiceMock());
  const fixture = magic.fixture(MyComponent, { param: 100 });
  return { fixture, childMocks, serviceMock };
}
it('should render with input', () => {
  const { fixture, serviceMock } = setup();
  expect(fixture.componentInstance.param).toBe(100);
  expect(serviceMock.load).toHaveBeenCalled();
});
```
**`componentMocks<C>(componentClass)`**
Declares `componentClass` as a mock component for a selector and returns an array that will be populated with all rendered mock instances **after** `fixture()` is called. Must be called before `fixture()`.
```typescript
// Define a mock component matching the selector you want to stub
@Component({ selector: 'lib-button', template: '' })
class MyButtonMock implements Partial<MyButtonComponent> {
  @Output() click = new EventEmitter();
}
function setup() {
  const magic = new NgMagicSetupTestBed();
  const buttons = magic.componentMocks(MyButtonMock);  // call before fixture
  const fixture = magic.fixture(ParentComponent, { param: 100 });
  const firstButton = buttons[0];                      // usable after fixture
  return { fixture, firstButton };
}
it('should react to child click', () => {
  const { firstButton, fixture } = setup();
  firstButton.click.emit();
  fixture.detectChanges();
  // assert parent reaction
});
```
**`directiveMocks<C>(directiveClass)`**
Returns all rendered directive instances after fixture creation. Same call-before-fixture pattern as `componentMocks`.
**`run<T>(fn)`**
Executes a factory function within Angular's injection context. Use this to instantiate classes that call `inject()` in their constructor or field initializers.
```typescript
class MyObject {
  private service = inject(MyService);  // requires injection context
  getValue() { return this.service.getValue(); }
}
it('should support inject()-based classes', () => {
  const magic = new NgMagicSetupTestBed();
  const serviceMock = magic.serviceMock(MyService);
  serviceMock.getValue.and.returnValue(42);
  const obj = magic.run(() => new MyObject());
  expect(obj.getValue()).toBe(42);
});
```
### Observables
**`observer<T>(observable$, name?)`**
Subscribes to an observable and returns a `SpyObserver<T>` for asserting emissions.
```typescript
const events$ = magic.observer(service.events$);
// trigger something
expect(events$.next).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ type: 'update' });
expect(events$.observations).toEqual([{ type: 'update' }]);
expect(events$.latest).toEqual({ type: 'update' });
```
---
## SpyObserver\<T\>
Returned by `magic.observer()`. Wraps an observable with Jasmine spies.
| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `next` | `jasmine.Spy` | Called on each emission |
| `error` | `jasmine.Spy` | Called on error |
| `complete` | `jasmine.Spy` | Called on completion |
| `observations` | `T[]` | Array of all emitted values |
| `latest` | `T` | Most recently emitted value |
---
## Standalone Functions
**`observe<T>(observable$, name?)`**
Standalone alternative to `magic.observer()`. Use when you don't have (or need) an `NgMagicSetupTestBed` instance.
```typescript
import { observe } from '@peejay-solutions/ng-magic-test-bed';
const spy = observe(myService.events$, 'events');
expect(spy.next).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedValue);
```
**`mock<S>(spySource?, mock?, dontSpy?)`**
Standalone alternative to `magic.objectMock()`. Creates a mock object from a class prototype without TestBed registration.
```typescript
import { mock } from '@peejay-solutions/ng-magic-test-bed';
const myMock = mock(MyService, { getData: () => [] });
// myMock has spies for all MyService methods; getData calls through to the provided fn
```
**`spyOnFunctionsOf(target, source?)`**
Converts all methods of `target` into Jasmine spies in place. Inherited methods are overwritten on the object itself (not on the prototype) to avoid side effects. An optional `source` can add extra spies from another class's prototype.
```typescript
import { spyOnFunctionsOf } from '@peejay-solutions/ng-magic-test-bed';
const instance = spyOnFunctionsOf(new MyService());
instance.doSomething('x');
expect(instance.doSomething).toHaveBeenCalledWith('x');
// Use when creating non-TestBed instances that still need spy tracking
const factoryMock = spyOnFunctionsOf(new MyFactory());
const serviceMock = spyOnFunctionsOf(new MyHelperService());
const sut = new MyService(factoryMock, serviceMock);
```
---
## IFactory Interface
Used by `factoryMock`. Any service with a `create(...args): I` method qualifies.
```typescript
interface IFactory<I> {
  create(...args: any[]): I;
}
```
